studies.label: FIERO versus Google Docs collaborative superhero-story writing

counts_source.locator: PDF p. 13, Section 4.1 (random assignment); PDF p. 41, Table 1 caption and note (questionnaire arm and total counts)

arms.name: FIERO
arms.description: Face-to-face collaborative writing with physical narrative cards, a shared FIERO interface, generated images, optional AI decision support, and final-story suggestions and polishing. The analyzed count is the questionnaire count (PDF p. 41, Table 1); people represented by the scored-story corpus are not identified. Arm-specific randomization counts are not separately reported.

arms.name: Control (Google Docs)
arms.description: Face-to-face collaborators draft, discuss, and integrate a superhero story in a shared Google Docs document, following the same narrative tasks and round timing. No AI or physical cards. The analyzed count is the questionnaire count (PDF p. 41, Table 1); people represented by the scored-story corpus are not identified. Arm-specific randomization counts are not separately reported.

studies.task: Teams of three collaboratively write a superhero story through hero, villain/scene, and weapon/climax rounds, then integrate the final narrative (PDF pp. 13-14, Section 4.1; PDF pp. 47-48, Appendix E).

ai_tool.name: FIERO: GPT-4 for decision support and final-story assistance; GPT-4o image model (gpt-4o-image) for images

notes: Reconciled on 2026-10-11 from the saved arXiv v1 PDF. The complete markdown conversion, including references and Appendices A-H, was read in consecutive chunks. Every cited numerical passage was checked with pymupdf against the PDF; quoted passages were also matched against extracted PDF text. All study and estimate counts, question, construct, unit, higher_is, outcome_with_ai and within_person fields were independently checked even where A and B agree. The study-level analyzed count and arm analyzed counts refer to questionnaires only. The participant headcount of the scored-story corpus is unreported, so estimate-level people counts remain null. Individual random assignment is explicitly stated (PDF p. 13); timing of team formation and allocation procedures are unstated. The teams reported on PDF p. 16 are not confirmed randomized clusters, and Tables 3-4 on PDF pp. 43-44 identify teams rather than experimental sessions. The task was offline, face-to-face collaborative superhero-story writing, so design_class is lab_rct and task_type is creative_writing. The sample comprises students and non-students, so population is mixed; country and assistance-model release years are unreported. The AI role spans image generation, decision support and refinement and is coded other (PDF p. 12; Appendix F). Both arms include human collaborators; the Google Docs condition is the no-AI baseline, so comparison_type is ai_vs_bau. FIERO combines AI with physical cards and a game interface, as acknowledged on PDF p. 34, Section 6.6.1. All eligible outcomes score the final stories produced with AI available and therefore answer with_ai, with immediate timing and outcome_with_ai=true. The study is between subjects; AB/BA reverses the judges' presentation order, not participants' treatment order, so within_person is null. Pair is the unit of LLM comparisons, not a diversity construct. The rubric supports overall_creativity for Creativity, elaboration for Development, other for Anthropomorphism, and usefulness for the remaining quality dimensions (PDF pp. 15-16 and 45-46). Higher values favor better creative-story quality, except Anthropomorphism, whose higher_is=other means more human-like and psychologically developed characters. Language Use scores fictional-story quality and is not an excluded argumentative/expository proficiency test. The screened outcomes S1-O1 through S1-O7 are all represented for each evaluator. Overall comparison and Overall Preference are separate reported summaries of the same form outcome and sample. The comparison script matched those summaries in reverse order: all flagged estimate-field discrepancies disappear after matching their actual labels and sections.
